sources.excerpt: "`pigeons add` writes a `Host` entry to your SSH config whose `ProxyCommand` runs `pigeons fly --stdio`, so `ssh` reaches the tunnel over that command's stdin and stdout."

Behaviors recorded in v2 (README at pinned commit): (1) opt-in anonymous telemetry: asks once on the first setup command (roost, fly, add, service install) in a terminal; nothing sent unless telemetry_enabled = true; endpoint counters sampled once a minute and pushed to iroh-services (relay usage, hole-punching success, bytes moved); the sending endpoint ID is visible to the collector; (2) `pigeons service install` installs a system service (systemd, launchd, Windows SCM) and the roost then runs as root, reading a machine-wide config (/etc/pigeons/config.toml or C:\ProgramData\pigeons\config.toml); (3) `pigeons add` writes a Host entry to ~/.ssh/config (README example output: "Pigeon route 'my-server' added to ~/.ssh/config"); (4) a dedicated keypair .ssh/pigeons_ed25519 is used; (5) security model: anyone holding the endpoint ID can reach the SSH port. M00 fixture rule (inference from CLAUDE.md boundaries): run with HOME pointed at a scratch directory, never run `service install`, and answer or preset telemetry off.

sources.note: Drift on main observed by `fetch_pins.py upstream` at 2026-10-09T05:36Z and again at 06:14Z (fix2/upstream1.json, final_upstream.json): the main-branch blob is 132b65548125543e14dee24854f2be2aeac7b33f, not the pinned blob 2428783ccc56531e1281ef056ed3b216539210e4. The pin is the commit permalink 3b75e60; `fetch` reads that commit and its blob sha1 matches. Quoted excerpt fragments still on main: 3/3. The commit that changed the path on main was not looked up (no GitHub API request). Claim re-read 2026-10-31 (M00-T02-fix4, docs/sources/drift-2026-10-31.md; first found by recheck3, claim-S34.out): changed, adjacent to the excerpted statements. The three quoted fragments are still on main (3/3) and the narrow statements hold (a bootstrap exchange can narrow a grant but not widen it; projects are not filesystem sandboxes). But the pin says ordinary pairing does not grant access-management or relay-management authority, while main says the default grant includes access and relay management, and that terminal:operate (a shell as the server's user) or orchestration:operate (can start a full-access agent) can mint a session with every scope through `t3 auth session issue`, so withholding management from the default would not be a boundary. Main also names the file-reading scope filesystem:read (the pin calls it orchestration:read) and adds that a URL minted before the grant was revoked keeps working until it expires. Disposition: qualification recorded. The immutable pin stays the experiment baseline; main's defaults are not promoted into any Heimdall contract; G07's authority-boundary investigation (plan.md section 3, G07: attempt privileged management as a limited client; pairing must not become unlimited owner authority) is retained, reopened on this point, and its owner re-reads the main section.

e6_facts: Inbox client observed natively (G03, 2026-10-06, tests/evidence/g03-win-env-inventory.json, record status verified): on the owner's Windows 11 Pro build 26300.9550 x86-64, C:\WINDOWS\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe reports "OpenSSH_for_Windows_9.5p2, LibreSSL 3.8.2", file version 9.5.6.3, sha256 0b8b5653141c6e02e8afc043d1703dcd6410f1606422ff3ba5eb52dc56a5cce9. Spec section 3.2 says Windows tests include "the installed Windows OpenSSH client"; the inbox build is Microsoft-distributed with Windows and has no release tag to pin. One host, one observation; not a floor.

Same host: the Win32-OpenSSH GitHub MSI was installed at C:\Program Files\OpenSSH (ssh.exe reports "OpenSSH_for_Windows_10.0p2 Win32-OpenSSH-GitHub, LibreSSL 3.8.2", file version 10.0.0.0, sha256 6890c128c86cc2c38aad9fcb32a82b851ff3d38c714a1f656b8e445d7cd5e1c6), first on PATH, and the ssh-agent and sshd services ran from it. Git for Windows 2.55.0.windows.3 bundles MSYS "OpenSSH_10.3p1, OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026". Both builds were compared only in some probes: P-W02 (SSH_AUTH_SOCK selection; the record has agent contact rows for both builds) and P-W03 (IdentityAgent forms) per docs/research/g03-windows-wsl.md section 0.1, and the five WSL Mode A probes P-A01-P-A05 (run r3-msi10, same status and criteria, section 0.2). The other executed native Windows probes used the inbox 9.5p2 only.

Both Microsoft builds report LibreSSL 3.8.2 in their version banner. The LibreSSL licence, and the licences of any other third-party component in the release binaries, are not recorded here: the LICENCE quoted above covers the openssh-portable source tree only. Microsoft's licence terms for the inbox Feature-on-Demand build are not recorded either.

escalations.summary: Suggested spec clarification, not a contradiction. Spec line 323 says remembered approvals do not keep private keys available after lock; S06 and S07 support that as written (unlock still required for key access). S07 also documents timed remembering (4/12/24 h) under which key APPROVALS stay in agent memory while 1Password is locked. A clarifying sentence distinguishing approvals from key availability would prevent misreading; wording is the spec owner's decision.
Spec says ssh -G evaluation may run Match exec; no single source sentence states this; it is an inference. Needs G07/G09 behavioral evidence, not a doc citation.

reopen_conditions: `fetch_pins.py compare` against docs/sources/fetch-baseline.json (or fetch-baseline-aux.json) classifies a source cited by a gate that is still open as CONTENT (normalized text changed), GONE (HTTP 404 or 410, after one confirming re-run) or MISSING; read docs/sources/snapshots/<id>.txt.gz to see what the pin said. primary_same=no is the off-pin flag (the second file does not reproduce the pinned primary hash): compare always prints such a line and exits 5 when nothing worse was found. Against the baseline, off-pin with class RAW_ONLY or MARKER_ONLY means the text equals the pin and only the raw bytes of a raw-primary source moved: that is pin maintenance (run `verify`, then re-pin with a dated note), not drift, and not a reopen. An off-pin normalized-primary source is CONTENT, so it is drift. MARKER_ONLY, and RAW_ONLY with primary_same=yes, are not drift. FETCH_FAILED means re-run, not drift, unless the same source is FETCH_FAILED on runs at least 24 h apart: then treat it as GONE and investigate. Dated dispositions of the 2026-10-31 drift (21 spec and 4 auxiliary CONTENT sources, 4 branch-drifted GitHub sources, 1 lost fragment): docs/sources/drift-2026-10-31.md.

`fetch_pins.py upstream` exits 2 (a GitHub source drifted on the branch its spec URL names and lost a quoted fragment or has none to check, or its file is gone), or exits 4 (drifted, quotes intact, claim not re-read) for a source cited by a gate that is still open and the re-read shows that the claim changed. Exit 4 does not show that the claim still holds. Before anyone relies on `main` for a source cited by a still-open gate, read the branch file against the claim and record the outcome (date, `claim re-read: holds` or `changed`) in the source's note; the pinned permalink stays the citation of record until then (on 2026-10-09 S16, S17, S18 and S34 had drifted on main with all fragments present; their claims were not re-read). Re-read on 2026-10-31 (M00-T02-fix4): S16 holds; S17 and S18 hold with qualifications; S34 changed adjacent to its excerpts (default grants), so G07's authority-boundary investigation is retained; S29 lost its Zig 0.16.0 fragment and is closed by the recorded G02 disposition (docs/sources/drift-2026-10-31.md).
